# typing.NamedTuple fails with non-literal arguments

## Description

I found an issue with `typing.NamedTuple` when using non-literal arguments. When trying to create a NamedTuple with variables instead of literals, it doesn't work correctly.

## Steps to Reproduce

```python
from typing import NamedTuple

# This works fine
Person = NamedTuple("Person", [("name", str), ("age", int)])

# But using variables doesn't work
name = "X"
fields = [("a", int), ("b", str), ("c", bytes)]
MyTuple = NamedTuple(name, fields)  # This fails

# Also fails with empty field list
Bar = NamedTuple("bar", [])
Bar()  # This doesn't work either
```

## Expected Results

The NamedTuple should be created successfully regardless of whether the arguments are literals or variables. Both examples should work the same way.

## Actual Results

When using variables instead of literals for the typename and fields arguments, the NamedTuple creation fails. Similarly, creating a NamedTuple with an empty field list also fails.

## Environment
- Python 3.10
- Latest version of typing module

I tried this in a simple script and it doesn't work as expected. The same code works fine when using collections.namedtuple, but fails with typing.NamedTuple.
</issue>
